title: Awakening
text:
Light enters and I clumsily ascend
+
+from dreams into the shared dream,
+
+and things regain their proper
+
+and expected place, and in the present
+
+the vague yesterday converges, vast
+
+and overwhelming: the age-old migrations
+
+of bird and man, the legions
+
+iron shattered, Rome and Carthage.
+
+
+The daily story also returns:
+
+my voice, my face, my fear, my fate.
+
+Ah, if that other awakening, death,
+
+should grant me time without memory
+
+of my name and all that I have been!
+
+Ah, if in that morning there were oblivion!
editorial_note: Waking is kept as an ascent from private dreams into the collective dream of history and identity; death becomes the hoped-for awakening into oblivion.

title: The Dream
text:
If sleep were (as they say) a
+
+truce, a pure repose of mind,
+
+why, if you are suddenly awakened,
+
+do you feel they have stolen a fortune from you?
+
+
+Why is it so sad to rise at dawn? The hour
+
+strips us of an inconceivable gift,
+
+so intimate it can be translated only
+
+into a drowsiness that waking gilds
+
+
+with dreams, which may well be broken
+
+reflections of the treasures of shadow,
+
+of a timeless realm that has no name
+
+
+and that day deforms in its mirrors.
+
+Who will you be tonight in the dark
+
+dream, on the other side of its wall?
editorial_note: Dream remains treasure, translation, and damaged reflection of a nameless realm; the final question addresses the unknown self beyond sleep’s wall.

title: James Joyce
text:
Within one human day are all the days
+
+of time, from that inconceivable
+
+first day of time, when a terrible
+
+God preordained the days and agonies,
+
+until that other day when the ubiquitous river
+
+of earthly time returns to its source,
+
+which is Eternity, and present,
+
+future, yesterday, and what is now mine go dark.
+
+Between dawn and night lies universal
+
+history: From night I see
+
+at my feet the pathways of the Hebrew,
+
+Carthage annihilated, Hell and Glory.
+
+Give me, Lord, courage and joy
+
+to scale the summit of this day.
editorial_note: One day contains sacred and universal history in a Joycean compression; the final prayer turns the cosmic scheme into the human labor of enduring a day.

title: Remorse
text:
I have committed the worst of sins
+
+a man can commit. I have not been
+
+happy. May the glaciers of oblivion
+
+drag me away and lose me, merciless.
+
+
+My parents engendered me for the beautiful
+
+and hazardous game of life,
+
+for earth, water, air, and fire.
+
+I failed them. I was not happy. Their youthful
+
+
+will was not fulfilled. My mind
+
+applied itself to the symmetrical contests
+
+of art, which interweaves trivialities.
+
+
+They bequeathed me courage. I was not brave.
+
+It does not leave me. Always at my side
+
+is the shadow of having been an unhappy man.
editorial_note: The confession remains severe and formally measured; naderías becomes trivialities, retaining the aged poet’s indictment of art beside the elemental game of life.

editorial_note: This separately hashed witness of “Remorse” preserves the same reviewed translation; its source differs only in the capitalization of the final line.

title: Another Version of Proteus
text:
Dweller in wary sands,
+        half god and half sea beast,
+        he knew nothing of memory, which bends
+        over yesterday and things that are lost.
+
+
+        Proteus suffered another torment,
+        no less cruel: to know what the future already holds,
+        the door that closes
+        forever, the Trojan and the Achaean.
+
+
+        Captured, he assumed the ungraspable
+        form of hurricane or pyre,
+        or golden tiger or panther,
+
+
+        or water invisible in water.
+        You too are made of inconstant
+        yesterdays and tomorrows. Meanwhile, before…
editorial_note: Proteus is defined by foresight rather than memory and by forms that evade capture; the unfinished temporal phrase remains suspended at the close.

title: A Key in Salonica
text:
Abarbanel, Farías, or Pinedo,
+        cast out of Spain by impious
+        persecution, still preserve
+        the key to a house in Toledo.
+
+
+        Free now of hope and fear,
+        they look upon the key as day declines;
+        in the bronze are yesterdays, distance,
+        weary gleam, and quiet suffering.
+
+
+        Today, when its door is dust, the instrument
+        is cipher of diaspora and wind,
+        akin to that other key of the sanctuary
+
+
+        someone hurled into the blue when the Roman
+        attacked with reckless fire,
+        and which a hand received in heaven.
editorial_note: Cifra remains cipher, joining symbol and encoded history; the domestic Sephardic key is linked to the legendary sanctuary key received by a heavenly hand.

title: Coronel Suárez
text:
High in the dawn rises the severe
+        face of metal and melancholy.
+        A dog slips along the pavement.
+        It is no longer night and not yet day.
+
+
+        Suárez looks upon his town and the farther
+        plain, the ranches, the paddocks,
+        the trails that weary the cattle drovers,
+        the patient planet that endures.
+
+
+        Behind the effigy I divine you,
+        O young captain who were master
+        of that battle which bent destiny:
+
+
+        Junín, resplendent as a dream.
+        At one edge of the vast South persists
+        that lofty thing, vaguely sad.
editorial_note: The statue, town, ancestor, and battle occupy one dawn; the final alta cosa preserves Borges’s deliberately impersonal monument, elevated and faintly mournful.
